recipes.name: Navy Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 6 large potatoes, peeled and quartered lengthwise
1 cup butter, divided, or more as needed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place the potato wedges in a bowl of water, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray. Melt 1/2 cup of butter in a small saucepan over low heat; pour it into a shallow dish. Mix flour, salt, and pepper in a second shallow dish. Roll potato wedges in the seasoned flour, then dip into the butter. Arrange potato wedges on the baking sheet. Melt and add more butter for dipping as you go along (the flour makes it thick).
Bake the wedges in the preheated oven until tender and golden brown, 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Navy Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Simple, buttery baked potato wedges have a crunchy flour coating.

review.reviewBody: Recipe is what it says a french fry potato with a slight "buttery crunchy coating." I followed the ingredients minus the black pepper. I cut the potatoes each into 8-10 potato wedges, and they did still take the full 40 minutes. And, I baked them on a foil lined sheet. I did half the recipe and it fit the whole baking sheet. I would say the full recipe would be more like 6 servings though. Interesting recipe! And, I wonder if my grandpa ate a french fry like these in the the Navy in WWII? Happy Veterans's Day though! And, thank you to all who have served this country.

This is a good recipe. I added Cajun spices and extra paprika in the flour mix. It gave it a good taste. I also used the air fryer. Y’all, this was yum yum good!!!!! I heated up the next day in the air fryer and it tasted even better the next day and more crunchy. Air fryer for life!

I don't recall ever having these during 6 years in the Navy, but with a name like that I had to try them. I made them according to the recipe except I added 1 tsp of cayenne pepper. That gave them just a bit of spice- if you like hot you can probably double that. These were pretty good and something a little different from plain your standard potatoes. I'll definitely make them again. To make things easier/neater, next time I'll try putting the flour mix in a plastic bag or tupperware bowl and toss the potatoes in it instead of rolling them in the mix. I'll also try tossing in the butter or pouring the butter over the floured potatoes instead of dipping them in the butter.
Easy and if you slice a little thinner you can easily have it done in 15-20 minutes. If you just want simple potatoes with a little crunch and butter flavor hard to beat. Thanks!
My family really enjoyed these. I used white rice flour and used margarine because I was out of butter. They were tender & crispy. Cooked on parchment and turned part way through.

This is a tried and true recipe in my home. I have made these at least a few dozen times. I use white rice flour without issue, because I’m gluten free. I’ve also made these many times with butter and many times with margarine and surprisingly they’re way better with margarine. Don’t get me wrong I’ll take them either way, but the oils in the margarine seem to help the potatoes brown and crisp.

Decent potatoes. They need more seasoning to suit my tastes. I was trying to replicate those potato wedges that KFC used to sell or what I call "gas station" potato wedges. This wasn't quite it, but close. It's probably a matter of seasonings as the texture was the same. There was a flour taste that wasn't toasty and needed to be. I didn't want them too thick and quartered was going to be too big to be bite sized when eating, so I cut the potatoes into 5 wedges instead of 4. They were still good sized. 2 potatoes made 3 servings at our house. The only thing I'd do differently is to turn them over during baking as the side touching the baking tray had a beautiful golden brown color and got a little crispy, while the others didn't. These were a good start in finding the secret to those "gas station" potato wedges, but aren't quite it. We ate them all so we liked them fine. It was easy to do, and a nice change from the usual french fries to go with our burgers.
Very good potato wedges! I used seasoned salt and added onion powder & garlic powder. 400 degrees for 40 mins flipping half way through.

The potatoes were crunchy and buttery. I liked them and we would certainly make them again. Next time, I will probably add extra spices as others have recommended. A good recipe to experiment with potatoes.
Love love LOVE this recipe. So versatile too. Added a bit of smoked paprika and a smidge of dill. Kids came back for seconds...and thirds.
I made this tonight, and thought it was very good. It took awhile to prepare and cook, but I'll do it again as it was a great side dish.

I’ve tried making these several times. First time following recipe exactly then alternatives for follow up attempts (less flour, more spices, precook potatoes in boiling water halfway). I really wanted this recipe to work, but no success. They just taste like uncooked flour to me. Might be ok if I could deep fry them, but I don’t have access to deep fryer on a boat.
I like it and made it many times, I experimented with some additional flavours, but it came out that the receipe is the best as it is
I used Emeril's Essence to give them more flavor. I did not try them but hubby said they were ok for a change but he would just as soon have a baked potato so they won't be worth the effort again.

Really good! I added an all purpose spice to the flour as other reviewers have and I did find my cookie sheet warped a bit during the cooking and some of the butter browned and the fries got pretty dark but DH preferred those so I guess it all worked out. Just keep a close eye out as the butter can burn before you know it.
Very easy and surprisingly good. I added a bit of cajun spice to the flour and it worked really well.
